correctness.rationale: Rational upper decompositions give upper bounds over every field where the model is defined. Any shorter characteristic-zero decomposition descends to a finitely generated Q-subfield, which embeds into C and contradicts Li. For reduction modulo p, the forbidden rank bounds are finite polynomial systems with Q-coefficients; their lack of complex points yields rational Nullstellensatz certificates, and clearing finitely many denominators preserves both lower-bound certificates and upper decompositions outside finitely many primes. The proof explicitly uses scalar-weighted symmetric rank, matching Lovitz.

originality.rationale: Li proves the exact double- and triple-copy ranks only over R and C, while Lovitz proves only the single copy over Q, R and C. The new claim transfers Li's exact gaps to every characteristic-zero field and to all but finitely many positive characteristics. No inspected published-finding corpus record or primary source states or implies this exact field-persistence conclusion for the low-dimensional gap-two and gap-three tensors.
residual_risks: The finite-exception spreading-out consequence may be regarded as standard folklore even though no covering statement was located for these tensors.
The exceptional primes are not identified, so the result does not compare with possible special behavior in small characteristics.
A specialist source using arithmetic geometry terminology not surfaced by the searches could contain an equivalent transfer statement.

value.rationale: Ground-field dependence is intrinsic in tensor-rank problems. Extending the first low-dimensional exact Comon gaps larger than one from R/C to every characteristic-zero field and almost every characteristic gives a natural arithmetic robustness theorem, rather than a routine numerical variant. It provides exact gap-two and gap-three examples across a much broader field class while clearly retaining a finite exceptional-prime limitation.
